subject.title: [Bug]: Slack `allowBots: true` silently drops all bot messages unless `allowFrom` contains an explicit owner user ID

question: Should Slack `allowBots: true` remain gated on an explicit owner ID, or should OpenClaw add a supported wildcard/escape-hatch behavior for bot-authored room messages?
rationale: The current behavior is documented and security-motivated, but it creates real message loss for wildcard allowlists; automation should not choose whether to relax a Slack authorization boundary.

options.title: Keep gate and add diagnostics
options.body: Preserve explicit-owner presence and add a visible doctor/setup/channel-status warning for `allowBots` with wildcard-only `allowFrom`, plus docs that name the supported config.

options.title: Add explicit permissive mode
options.body: Introduce a clearly named opt-in mode such as `allowBots: "all"` with loop-protection and security docs so users can choose the tradeoff without weakening the default.

options.title: Treat wildcard as owner presence
options.body: Make `allowFrom: ["*"]` satisfy the current gate, accepting that bot-authored room messages can reach the agent whenever the channel is otherwise allowed.

recommendation.title: Keep gate and add diagnostics
recommendation.body: Preserve explicit-owner presence and add a visible doctor/setup/channel-status warning for `allowBots` with wildcard-only `allowFrom`, plus docs that name the supported config.

likelyOwner.reason: The owner-presence behavior appears to originate from steipete's 8b665e0d7066 Slack hardening commit, making him the strongest available routing owner for this security/UX tradeoff.
